en: Never throw aerosol cans into a fire because the heated gas inside expands and causes the metal can to explode.
Drinking seawater dehydrates your body because its high salt concentration draws water out of your cells through osmosis.
Leaving wet iron tools outside causes a chemical change called oxidation, creating rust that weakens the metal.
Boiling water for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria and makes it safe to drink.
Never mix bleach with other liquid cleaning solutions because it can cause a chemical reaction that releases toxic gas.
Never touch dry ice with bare hands because its extremely cold solid carbon dioxide causes severe frostbite.
Milk turns sour and forms solid lumps when bacteria cause a chemical change that produces lactic acid.
Keep rubbing alcohol away from open flames because its high flammability means it catches fire very easily.
Natural gas is odorless, but utility companies add a chemical called mercaptan so you can smell dangerous leaks.
Baking powder releases carbon dioxide gas when heated, causing cake batter to expand and become fluffy.
Metal pots have plastic handles because plastic is a thermal insulator that prevents your hands from burning.
HEPA air filters trap solid dust particles and pollen from the gas mixture we call indoor air.
